changes.after: Let an input's type choose between methods with the same name.

before: Method overloading defines methods with the same name but different parameter lists. A signature distinguishes those input lists; changing only the return type is not enough.
For the two overloads here, an int argument selects the int version and a string argument selects the string version. The compiler chooses before either body runs.

A class groups members. This example uses static methods, callable through the class name without creating an object. public makes them accessible from the calling code. Classes and access rules are taught fully later.
"4" is a string while 4 is an int. The printed spelling may look similar, but overload selection uses their types.
Expected behavior from this example: number then text. This expected result is a reasoned prediction until a compiler test is recorded.

Optional local transfer task: Call both overloads with new values. Then explain why two methods differing only in return type would not give the compiler a choice from these arguments. You may trace it on paper if no C# toolchain is installed; reading completion does not certify a run.
after: An overload is a method that shares its name with another method but has different inputs. Changing only the return type is not enough to create an overload.
These two Make methods take different types: int and string. The compiler chooses the matching method from the argument's type.
A class groups related code. Label is the class name here. Its two methods both return text. Later lessons explain classes in more detail.
static lets these methods be called through Label without creating a Label object. public allows the calling code to use them.
The program prints number, then text. The first call supplies an int. The second supplies a string.
4 is a number. "4" is text, even though it contains a digit. The type decides which of these overloads runs.

choices: The int version because 8 looks numeric.
The string version because the supplied value is text.
Both versions run and their results merge.
before.explanation: Quotes make the argument a string; the string overload is selected.

after.question: Change the first argument to "8" with quotes. Which Make method runs?
after.explanation: Quotes make the argument a string, so C# selects Make(string value).
